answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake before it can endorse work or claim rewards. A newcomer sparrow may earn trust through verified, useful contributions, but cannot multiply influence merely by minting accounts: each account locks scarce capital, and coordinated accounts risk losing it when endorsements are proven fraudulent. The nectar of this design is that honest participation stays open while attackers pay an opportunity cost and face forfeiture; zephyr-like disposable identities are no longer free.
